summary: The milestone completed 14 synthesis-only experiments in 0.6 minutes. No compute-bound experiments ran, so the GPU snapshot cannot support a compute-task utilization or DualGPURunner finding.
bottlenecks_identified: No runtime bottleneck is established. Timing used disk-mtime reconstruction because the live git-log path found no commits, which prevents task-phase attribution.
improvements_suggested: Record monotonic start, phase, and finish timestamps in each experiment artifact so future retrospectives can use live timings instead of disk-mtime reconstruction.
Persist task classification and model-concurrency metadata with each timing record so compute-bound status and parallel-model eligibility are auditable.
When compute-bound work runs, attach task-window GPU samples and runner-dispatch metadata to its record so GPU efficiency and DualGPURunner engagement can be evaluated.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add monotonic per-task and per-phase timestamps to experiment artifacts.
Store task classification and model-concurrency metadata beside timing data.
Capture task-window GPU samples and runner-dispatch metadata for compute-bound work.
meta_reflection: The evidence supports a process diagnosis, not a compute diagnosis: all 14 runs were synthesis-only and total wall time was 0.6 minutes. A nonzero savings estimate would not be supported, so estimated time savings is 0% until direct timing identifies avoidable work.
